questions.q: The retention head's request contains no target column, feature list, or metric. What does that tell you about real data science projects?
options: The request is badly written and should be sent back
A model can be built without a target
Metrics should be chosen only after seeing results
Turning a business request into a precise prediction problem is part of the data scientist's job
questions.explain: Business requests are rarely specified as targets, features, and metrics. Scoping them is the first real task, and lessons 2 and 3 cover it.

questions.q: Why is the capstone dataset generated from a fixed seed?
options: So the model is guaranteed to reach a high score
Because SQLite cannot store random numbers
So everyone regenerates the identical database and can check their numbers against the lessons
To hide the messy data problems
questions.explain: A fixed seed makes the synthetic data reproducible, so the counts printed by the script can be compared with the lesson before you go on.

questions.q: The customers table has 4,040 rows but only 4,000 distinct customer_id values. What is the most likely explanation, and what does the audit call it?
options: 40 duplicate customer rows that must be removed on customer_id
40 customers changed plans; a valid history
SQLite rounds customer IDs
40 customers have no orders
questions.explain: COUNT(*) minus COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) gives 40 duplicate rows. Duplicates would double-count those customers if left in.

questions.q: Why can text comparison in SQL not be trusted to order the signup_date column?
options: SQL cannot compare text
The column mixes formats such as 2024-03-13 and 28/08/2023, so string order is not date order
Dates are stored as integers
The column is always sorted already
questions.explain: 855 signup dates are not in YYYY-MM-DD format. Text comparison only matches date order when every value uses that same ISO layout, so the dates need parsing first.

questions.q: What is the purpose of auditing the tables with SQL before modeling?
options: To improve model accuracy directly
To delete the raw data
To find and document problems such as duplicates, impossible values, and mixed formats before they leak into results
To avoid using Python later
questions.explain: Cheap checks reveal what must be fixed and give you before-and-after counts for the cleaning rules. Building on an un-audited table risks silently wrong results.
